extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies, NEPA practitioners, and environmental counsel preparing or reviewing NEPA documents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how agencies must handle mitigation, monitoring, limitations on pre-decisional actions, and the adoption of other agencies' EISs/EAs/CE determinations under revised CEQ NEPA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROD certification regarding consideration of alternatives and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the separate certification requirement in the ROD that the agency considered all submitted alternatives, information, and analyses (40 CFR 1502.17); the decision maker's signature on the ROD is sufficient to indicate consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ considers the separate certification redundant and potentially misleading; agencies are entitled to a presumption of regularity under general administrative law rather than by NEPA-specific certification. The certification provision could suggest the agency did not consider elements such as comments and responses; therefore CEQ removes the paragraph requiring this certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to incorporate mitigation for environmental justice effects (§1505.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are encouraged to incorporate into their decisions mitigation measures addressing significant adverse human health and environmental effects that disproportionately and adversely affect communities with environmental justice concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an encouragement/policy statement, not a binding requirement. CEQ finalized the language to add 'into its decision' and removed 'adverse' after 'significant' (because 'significant effects' are by definition adverse). The change codifies CEQ's longstanding position that agencies should, as a policy matter, mitigate significant adverse effects, with particular focus on disproportionate effects on environmental justice communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a monitoring and compliance plan is required (§1505.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency must prepare and publish a monitoring and compliance plan for mitigation when (1) the analysis of the reasonably foreseeable effects of a proposed action in an EA or EIS is based on implementation of mitigation, and (2) the agency incorporates the mitigation into its ROD, FONSI, or separate decision document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies only where the agency's effects analysis relies on mitigation being implemented (i.e., mitigation is the basis for concluding effects are not reasonably foreseeable or not significant). It does not require such a plan for every NEPA action or every decision that includes mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement for monitoring and compliance plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must publish the monitoring and compliance plan when one is required under §1505.3(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although publication was implied previously because plans would be completed with RODs or FONSIs, CEQ explicitly requires publication to avoid confusion and increase transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the monitoring and compliance plan (§1505.3(c)(1) items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring and compliance plans should include: a description of the mitigation measures; the parties responsible for monitoring and implementation; how the information will be made publicly available, as appropriate; the anticipated timeframe for implementing and completing the mitigation; the standards for compliance with the mitigation; and how the mitigation will be funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed these specific content items to give agencies flexibility to tailor plans to mitigation complexity. CEQ declined to mandate that 'standards' explicitly address 'effectiveness' of mitigation, noting agencies evaluate effectiveness as part of NEPA and may use adaptive management where there is uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailoring and level of detail for monitoring and compliance plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may tailor monitoring and compliance plans to the complexity of the mitigation, but plans should contain sufficient detail to inform participating and cooperating agencies and the public about relevant considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested relevant considerations include magnitude of environmental effects subject to mitigation, degree to which mitigation is innovative, technical or other implementation challenges, time frame for implementation and monitoring, and other facts supporting determination that mitigation will be implemented. Where multiple agencies are involved, lead and cooperating agencies should collaboratively develop a plan that defines roles and avoids duplication. Agencies should leverage existing monitoring plans from other authorities rather than duplicate efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of monitoring and compliance plans for reliance on mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: A monitoring and compliance plan provides reasonable certainty that mitigation measures relied upon in the effects analysis will be implemented, supporting an agency's conclusion (e.g., that a FONSI is appropriate) where the analysis assumes mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If implementation of mitigation is not reasonably foreseeable, the agency cannot appropriately base effects analysis on that mitigation. The plan addresses concerns that mitigation commitments are sometimes not carried out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring information and supplementation / ongoing actions (§1505.3(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information developed through a monitoring and compliance plan does not, by itself, require an agency to supplement its environmental documents unless the underlying action is incomplete or ongoing and supplementation criteria are otherwise met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarified that the existence or implementation of a monitoring plan alone should not induce supplementation, to avoid perverse incentives (e.g., adopting less effective monitoring to avoid supplementation). CEQ also added that ongoing implementation of a monitoring plan alone is not an incomplete or ongoing Federal action that triggers supplementation under §§1501.5(h) or 1502.9(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies' evaluation of mitigation effectiveness and adaptive management
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies appropriately evaluate mitigation effectiveness as part of the NEPA process and may rely on techniques such as adaptive management to address substantial uncertainty about effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to require explicit standards of effectiveness in the monitoring plan contents, since agencies already evaluate effectiveness and can address uncertainty via adaptive management plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkage between monitoring/compliance plan and enforcement/mitigation summary (§1505.2(c) cross-reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring and compliance plans are related to requirements directing agencies to adopt and summarize a monitoring and enforcement program for any enforceable mitigation requirements or commitments in a ROD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations aim to provide consistency in content, increase transparency in disclosure of mitigation measures, and give the public and decision makers relevant information about mitigation implementation and compliance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on actions during NEPA process (§1506.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may authorize certain activities by applicants while NEPA is ongoing only if such activities do not have an adverse environmental impact and do not limit the choice of reasonable alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ added clarification that the Federal agency must notify the applicant that the agency retains discretion to select any reasonable alternative or the no-action alternative regardless of any activity the applicant has taken prior to conclusion of the NEPA process. CEQ changed terminology to 'applicant' for consistency. The intent is to preserve NEPA integrity while allowing applicants some flexibility to make business decisions at their own risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of 'required' for programmatic environmental reviews (§1506.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ retained the word 'required' in paragraph (c) and reverted to the phrasing 'environmental review for a program' to align with longstanding 1978 regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ notes that the principles in paragraph (c) remain: agencies must comply with NEPA for specific Federal actions before taking the action and cannot engage in activities that prejudice the outcome of the NEPA process. 'Programmatic environmental document' remains defined broadly and is not limited to program reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption allowed when actions are 'substantially the same' (§1506.3 general standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt another agency's EIS, EA, or CE determination (or portion thereof) when the adopting agency independently reviews the document and concludes it meets the standards for an adequate statement and the adopting agency's NEPA procedures, and the actions are substantially the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'substantially the same' standard facilitates efficiency because agency actions relating to the same overall project can differ (e.g., funding vs permitting) yet adoption may still be appropriate when the underlying activity analyzed is the same. Adoption should be done 'consistent with this section.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review and consistency with adopting agency procedures for adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Before adopting another agency's NEPA document, the adopting agency must independently review it to determine it meets CEQ regulations and the adopting agency's NEPA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ rejects the argument this is unduly burdensome; ensuring consistency with the adopting agency's procedures is codification of longstanding practice. Agencies are not required to wait to update procedures before adopting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation or reevaluation when adopting an older document (§1502.9 cross-reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the adopting agency determines that the EIS or EA may require supplementation or additional analysis (for example due to new or updated data), the agency may supplement or reevaluate the document consistent with §1502.9 (for EISs) or §1501.5(h) (for EAs) and document why supplementation is or is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the action is not substantially the same and supplemental analysis is necessary, the adopting agency should treat the EIS as a draft, prepare additional analysis, and publish a new draft EIS for notice and comment. The final rule replaces 'requires supplementation' with 'may require supplementation consistent with §1502.9' to cross-reference existing supplementation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of cooperating agency and cooperating agency adoption without republication (§1506.3(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A cooperating agency may adopt an EIS for an action it did not anticipate at the time the EIS was issued (e.g., a later funding decision) and may issue a ROD adopting the lead agency's EIS without republication, subject to the 'substantially the same' standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarified this provision to ensure it applies where the cooperating agency does not issue a joint or concurrent ROD consistent with §1505.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of EAs and CE determinations (paragraphs (c) and (d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard for adoption of an EA mirrors the standard for adoption of an EIS: an adopting agency may adopt another agency's EA, supplement or reevaluate it as necessary, and issue its FONSI if appropriate. Adoption of CE determinations likewise requires that the adopting agency's proposed action be substantially the same as the action analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarified that references to 'EA' mean final EAs (since regulations do not require both draft and final EAs). Adoption of a draft EA by another agency is appropriately handled via incorporation by reference. CEQ also revised paragraph (d) title to include 'determinations' and clarified that adoption means adopting another agency's determination that a CE applies to a particular proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public transparency when adopting another agency's NEPA document
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting another agency's EA/EIS/CE determination, agencies should ensure transparency by documenting any additional analysis, reevaluation, or supplementation decisions and, where appropriate, making the adopting agency's reasoning publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ finalized provisions allowing adoption while preserving opportunities for public engagement where actions are not substantially the same or additional analysis is needed; CEQ declined to require that agencies update procedures before using adoption.
